q: Fasting (Sawm) during the sacred month of ____ is the fourth pillar of Islam. (P3)
explain: During Ramadan, Muslims abstain from food and drink from dawn until sunset.

q: The meal eaten by Muslims before dawn to begin the daily fast is called ____. (P3)
explain: Sahur is the blessed pre-dawn meal before Fajr.

q: The meal eaten at sunset to break the fast is called ____. (P3)
explain: Iftar is traditionally initiated by eating dates and drinking water.

q: The annual obligatory charitable contribution given to help the poor is ____. (P3)
explain: Zakat (2.5% of qualifying wealth) purifies wealth and aids the vulnerable.

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Adam (AS) in Islamic heritage?
options: the first human being and first prophet created by Allah
explain: Prophet Adam (AS) was the first human being and first prophet created by Allah.

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Ibrahim (AS) in Islamic heritage?

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Musa (AS) in Islamic heritage?

explain: Prophet Musa (AS) was the prophet who spoke with Allah (Kalimullah) and received the Tawrat.

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Isa (AS) in Islamic heritage?
options: the noble prophet born miraculously to Maryam who received the Injil
explain: Prophet Isa (AS) was the noble prophet born miraculously to Maryam who received the Injil.

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Nuh (AS) in Islamic heritage?
options: the prophet who built the Ark to save believers from the great deluge
explain: Prophet Nuh (AS) was the prophet who built the Ark to save believers from the great deluge.

q: Prophetic history (P3): Who was Prophet Dawud (AS) in Islamic heritage?
options: the prophet-king who received the holy Psalms (Zabur)
